question: If the length of a chord, drawn at a distance of 21 cm from the centre of a circle, is 40 cm, then the radius (in cm) of the circle is:
solution:
Given:

Chord = 40cm 

Distance from centre to chord = 21 cm

Concept:

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of the chord bisects the chord in two equal parts. 

Pythagoras Theorem:

OA² = OD² + AD²

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/331d4557693c23facd62eeb677f12903e75ed3ef6343024df77bfe01617fe79b.png] 

Let AB be the chord of length 40 cm. 

⇒ OD be the perpendicular distance 

⇒ AO be the radius of the circle 

OA2 = OD2 + AD2

⇒ OA2 = 212 + (40/2)²

⇒ OA2 = 441 + 400 

⇒ OA2= 841

OA = √841

OA = 29

**The radius (in cm) of the circle is 29.**
